# Panic and assert sites

<!-- Generated by scripts/panic_sites.py render from docs/inventory/panics.tsv and scripts/panic-conditions.json. Edit the conditions file, not this page. -->

Every call from a kernel routine to `panic`, `cmn_err`, `assfail` or `nopanicdebugger` in the linked IRIX 6.5.30 kernels IP27, IP30 and IP35 that the panics table lists as in scope. The 6.5.22 release has no linked kernel yet, so it has no rows here.

Each row gives the call address, the callee, the message the call passes, and the condition under which the call runs. The message is read from the binary: the register value at the call, followed to a string in the file-backed data. `cmn_err` takes its level in a0 and its format in a1; `panic` takes its format in a0; `assfail` takes the failed expression in a0, the file name in a1 (not copied, it names a source file) and the line number in a2.

Grades: a message that is shown is established from the binary. `not resolved` means the scan could not follow the register: it is set on two paths that join before the call, or it comes from a pointer the routine loads at run time. A condition is established when the branch that decides the call was read in the disassembly; `not established` means no branch in the listing reaches the call.

Counts: 890 call sites in 253 routines; 50 have a written condition, 840 do not yet.
